To the FOIA Officer for Village Of Niles Illinois:

Pursuant to Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I request the following records:

All emails sent or received from October 26, 2022 through the date of the search that contain "Flock" or "ALPR" in the subject line, body or any attachment, by the following Village of Niles accounts (including any other account they used for Village or Niles Police Department business):
- the Village President and Board of Trustees
- the Village Manager and Assistant Village Manager
- the Village Clerk
- the Chief of Police, Deputy Chiefs, Commanders and Chief of Detectives
- the Police Department's ALPR administrator(s)
- Finance or purchasing staff who handled the Flock contracts

Excluded: automated alert and notification emails generated by the Flock system, and newsletters and mass mailings that no listed account replied to or forwarded.

Each email is produced in full: sender, all recipients including CC and BCC, date and time sent, subject line, body and attachments.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

If any fees apply, notify me of the estimated cost before charges are incurred. Records should be provided in electronic format, native and with metadata intact.

If any portion of this request is denied, please identify the specific exemption relied upon for each withheld record and provide an index of what is withheld.

A response is required within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

== BACKGROUND ==

A Flock camera records everyone who drives past it: plate, time and location, plus what Flock calls "Vehicle Fingerprint" details such as "bumper stickers, decals, and roof racks." According to the Niles Police Department's own Flock transparency portal, its 21 cameras logged 993,334 unique vehicles in the 30 days before October 13, 2026.

Since January 1, 2024, Illinois law (625 ILCS 5/2-130) has barred sharing that data for immigration enforcement or to penalize people seeking reproductive care. It also bars sharing with any out-of-state agency that has not first signed a written declaration promising not to.

Niles' own records show:
- January 31, 2024: Niles was sharing its cameras with 364 agencies, 43 of them outside Illinois.
- March 18, 2024: asked for every out-of-state declaration it had received, the Village answered, "We have no documents related to this request."
- May 30, 2025: Niles was sharing with 1,094 agencies, about 630 outside Illinois, including U.S. Border Patrol and the US Postal Inspection Service.
- June 2024 to February 2026: agencies Niles shared with ran 685 searches of Niles cameras logged for immigration enforcement.
- May 9, 2025: a Texas sheriff's search logged "had an abortion, search for female" reached Niles cameras.
- October 13, 2026: the transparency portal lists only Illinois agencies.


- WHAT OTHER AGENCIES SEARCHED NILES FLOCK CAMERAS FOR - 

Every search below is in Niles' own Flock network audits (June 2024 to February 2026), which list searches by other agencies that reached Niles cameras. Unless noted, every agency below was on Niles' May 30, 2025 sharing list with direct access to Niles cameras. Reasons are quoted as officers typed them.

Immigration enforcement (Illinois law bars sharing plate reader data for this):
- Louisville Metro KY PD: 138 searches logged "ERO" (ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations), February 28 to March 13, 2025.
- Richmond VA PD: 135 searches logged "ero" or "ICE ERO," March to June 2025.
- Houston TX PD: 114 searches logged "immigration," July 2024 to March 2025.
- Michigan State Police: 69 searches, including "Assist border patrol" and "USBP Immigration Investigation," January to May 2025.
- Palos Heights IL PD: 24 searches logged "Immigration violation," January 27 to 28, 2025.
- Matteson IL PD: 19 searches logged "HSI FCC Criminal Immigration" and similar, June 2025.
- Brownstown Township MI PD: "Immigration Enforcement (Border Patrol Assist - Agent Carlson)," 2025.
- Sevierville TN PD: "DEPORTATION ORDER," June 2025.
- Fishers IN PD: "Develop own PC for stops, ID occupants. Likely illegal Chileans or Columbians, verify IDs. Contact ICE to confirm," May 2025.
- An account named "[Federal] US Border Patrol [Inactive]": 24 searches logged "USBP/HSI," June 9, 2025, ten days after the date of a Niles sharing list that included U.S. Border Patrol.

Abortion:
- Johnson County TX Sheriff's Office: "had an abortion, search for female," May 9, 2025, across 83,345 cameras, including Niles'. Johnson County was not on Niles' sharing list; the search most likely came through Flock's nationwide lookup.

Protest surveillance:
- Springfield OH PD: 64 searches logged "protest," September 28 to 30, 2024.
- Skokie IL PD: 18 searches logged "Protest," October 7 to 8, 2024.
- Plover WI PD: 8 searches logged "trump rally POI" (person of interest), September 7, 2024.
- Lisle IL PD: "protest bulletin," October 20, 2025.
- Morristown TN PD: "Suspicious Protester Vehicle 'No Kings'," June 16, 2025.
- Kalamazoo MI PD: "ANTIFA," August 2024.

Ethnic slurs as search reasons (566 searches by 58 agencies Niles shared with):
- Rosemont IL PD: 291 searches logged "G*psy," July to September 2025.
- Highland Park IL PD: 37 searches logged "g*psy crew," August 13, 2025.
- Palos Heights IL PD: 28 searches logged "G*psy Concrete Scam" and "G*psy Vehicle," September 2024.
- Evanston IL PD: "G*PSY WOMEN ROMANIAN THEFT," August 2025.
- McCook IL PD: "need a traffic stop to ID occupants. Develop your own PC... Related to Romanian travelers," July 2025.
- Skokie IL PD: "g*psy," May 2025, and "t286132 g*psies," October 20, 2025.

Joke and personal reasons:
- Lake County IN Sheriff's Office: "LMAO." Chicago IL PD: "Hahah." Goshen IN PD: "Just because." Gurnee IL PD: "dude wheres my car."
- Houston TX PD: "my car." Moline IL PD: "Testing using personal plate." Greenfield WI PD: "personal."

No real reason at all:
- Houston TX PD: 15,994 searches logged "s." Posen IL PD: 13,694 logged "na."
- Creve Coeur IL PD: 8,079 searches, almost all logged "R." Its chief resigned in August 2026 amid allegations he used the village's Flock cameras to track his ex-wife. Creve Coeur is still on Niles' sharing list today.


- NILES POLICE'S OWN SEARCHES -

The Niles Police Department's own Flock audit logs (January 2024, and June 2024 to February 2026) list 16,646 searches by Niles users. Niles Police Department Policy 435 limits ALPR access to "legitimate law enforcement purposes only, such as when the data relate to a specific criminal investigation." The logs show:
- 438 searches logged "zz," "zzz" or "zzzz" as the reason, by two Niles PD Flock users: Alex Wolinski (313, November 25, 2024 to November 14, 2025) and Victor Martinez (125, January 28 to December 7, 2025). Five of Wolinski's reached more than 6,000 networks, including four logged "zzzz" on April 22 and 23, 2025.
- 1,468 searches in all with no meaningful reason. Besides "zz":
  - Kyle Krogstad typed "police" as the reason on all 204 of his searches, July 2024 to November 2025.
  - Liam Ryan typed "case" 247 times, January 2024 to January 2026.
  - Kevin Hernandez typed "." 86 times, May to November 2025.
  - Alex Wolinski also typed "x," "xx," "xxx," "xxxx" or longer strings of x's 212 times, including seven "xx" searches on March 7 and 10, 2025 that each reached more than 6,000 networks.
  - 48 searches were left with Flock's placeholder text "Case Type."
- 11,859 of 15,932 searches since June 2024 (74%) with no case number.
- 68 searches logged as traffic, driving or parking matters. Christopher Koch logged 40 as "traffic" and 4 as "parking complaint."
- 96 searches run for other agencies, including "Maywood homicide" (77), "chicago assist" (11) and "lyons pd assist" (3).
- 16 "convoy" searches, which find vehicles traveling together, September to December 2025. Ten were logged with the placeholder "Case Type," by Michael Oracion (4), Kevin Regal (3), Kelly Eckardt (2) and Andrew Mendez (1).


- WHERE NILES CONTRADICTS ITSELF -

The Niles Police Department's Flock transparency portal (<https://transparency.flocksafety.com/niles-il-pd>, checked October 13, 2026) and its own ALPR policy (Niles PD Policy 435) make promises that the Village's own records contradict.

Portal: "Prohibited Uses: Immigration enforcement."
Records: Niles shared its cameras with U.S. Border Patrol, and agencies Niles shared with ran 685 searches of Niles cameras logged for immigration enforcement, including "ICE ERO," "Assist border patrol" and "DEPORTATION ORDER."

Portal: "Prohibited Uses: ... traffic enforcement."
Records: the portal's own search log shows a Niles police search on September 20, 2026 with the offense type "Traffic Infraction." Niles' audit logs show 68 more searches logged as traffic, driving or parking matters, July 2024 to January 2026.

Portal: "Prohibited Uses: ... usage based solely on a protected class (i.e. race, sex, religion)."
Records: agencies Niles shared with ran 566 searches of Niles cameras using "g*psy" or "Romanian" as the reason.

Portal: "Prohibited Uses: ... Personal use."
Records: agencies Niles shared with logged searches of Niles cameras as "my car," "personal" and "Testing using personal plate." Creve Coeur, whose chief is accused of tracking his ex-wife, remains a sharing partner.

Portal: "All system access requires a valid law enforcement purpose and is stored indefinitely."
Records: agencies Niles shared with ran 180,847 searches of Niles cameras with reasons like "s," "na," "x," "." and "test." The portal's own public search log has no reason column at all, only a dropdown offense type, and drops every search after 30 days.

Portal: "Nothing is shared automatically. Participation is opt-in."
Records: Niles opted in to sharing with 1,094 agencies by May 2025, including Border Patrol. Niles' 2024 order form includes "Nationwide Network (LP Lookup Only)," which "Allows agencies to look up license plates on all cameras opted in to the nationwide Flock network." A Texas sheriff who was never on Niles' list still searched Niles cameras for a woman who "had an abortion."

Portal: "Sharing Network Data With" lists 475 agencies, all in Illinois.
Records: in May 2025 the list had 1,094 agencies, about 630 outside Illinois, and in March 2024 the Village had no out-of-state declarations on file. The portal shows only today's list. It says nothing about who had access before, or when that changed.

Policy 435.5(b): access is "for legitimate law enforcement purposes only, such as when the data relate to a specific criminal investigation."
Records: Alex Wolinski and Victor Martinez logged 438 searches as "zz," "zzz" or "zzzz." Kyle Krogstad gave "police" as the reason for every one of his 204 searches. In all, 1,468 Niles searches had no meaningful reason, and 74% of searches since June 2024 had no case number.

Policy 435.7: ALPR data "may be shared only" after the other agency "makes a written request," which must be "reviewed by the Administration Deputy Chief or the authorized designee and approved," with "the approved request ... retained on file." Before sharing out of state, the department "shall also ensure" it has received the agency's written declaration under 625 ILCS 5/2-130.
Records: Niles gave direct access to its cameras to 1,094 agencies by May 2025, about 630 of them out of state. In March 2024 the Village said it had no out-of-state declarations at all.

Board, May 24, 2022: Trustee Niedermaier calls Flock "a passive system currently" that "must be triggered for us to use it."
Records: the capital request the Board approved that night offered "convoy analysis." Niles officers ran 16 convoy searches in fall 2025, ten of them logged "Case Type."

Board, May 24, 2022: Trustee Niedermaier, after talking with the police chief, says the cameras are used "largely" for "stolen vehicles and Amber Alerts."
Portal: in its own 30-day search log, 77 of 146 Niles police searches were for drugs. Stolen vehicles accounted for 14.


- PEOPLE INVOLVED -

From the Village's own minutes and memos:

May 24, 2022: the first Flock contract (Village Board, consent agenda item 12.w)
- Requested by the Niles Police Department.
- Moved by Trustee Dean Strzelecki, a former Niles police chief. Seconded by Trustee Craig Niedermaier.
- Voting yes: Trustees John C. Jekot, Danette O'Donovan Matyas, Craig Niedermaier and Dean Strzelecki.
- Absent: President George D. Alpogianis and Trustee Joe Lo Verde.
- Trustee Matyas chaired the meeting as President Pro Tem.
- Earlier, on February 22, 2022, Trustee Strzelecki reported to the Board that the Public Safety Committee had heard the Police Department's case for "an enhancement to the Village's current license plate reader program including a new provider and additional units."

December 27, 2023: the early renewal
- Chief of Detectives Michael Boba recommends a new five-year Flock contract in a memo to Chief of Police Luis C. Tigera.

June 10, 2024: the state-funded cameras (Public Safety Committee)
- Chaired by Trustee Dean Strzelecki.
- Chief of Police Luis C. Tigera presents the $50,000 grant for 8 more Flock cameras.
- Moved by Fire Chief Feld, seconded by citizen member Fidanza, "with all voting members approving."

June 25, 2024: the contract is ratified (Village Board, consent agenda item 10.n)
- Memo from Chief of Police Luis C. Tigera.
- Moved by Trustee Danette O'Donovan Matyas. Seconded by Trustee Marryann Warda.
- Voting yes: President George D. Alpogianis and Trustees John C. Jekot, Danette O'Donovan Matyas, Craig Niedermaier and Marryann Warda.
- Absent: Trustees Morgan Dubiel and Dean Strzelecki.

April 28, 2026: the FY2027 budget, which keeps $34,396 a year for the plate reader program
- Moved by Trustee Dean Strzelecki. Seconded by Trustee Marryann Warda.
- Voting yes: Trustees Susan DeBartolo, Craig Niedermaier, Dean Strzelecki and Marryann Warda.
- Absent: Trustee Mody.

Trustee Craig Niedermaier voted yes all three times: the 2022 contract, the 2024 ratification and the 2026 budget. Trustee Dean Strzelecki moved the 2022 contract and the 2026 budget, and chaired the 2024 committee meeting that recommended more cameras. No trustee voted no on any of them.


- A HISTORY OF FLOCK SAFETY ALPR CAMERAS IN NILES -

Unless another source is linked, everything below comes from the Village of Niles' own agendas, packets, minutes, budgets, meeting video, public records responses and Flock transparency portal.

2019
- The Niles Police Department's 2019 Annual Report says its existing license plate readers were "made possible by a grant from ComEd." (<https://www.vniles.com/DocumentCenter/View/9563/2019-Annual-Report-PDF>, p. 41)

February 2022
- "Flock Safety LPR (Police)" appears on the February 18, 2022 Public Safety Committee agenda. (<https://www.vniles.com/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Agenda/_02182022-2269>)

April 26, 2022
- A commenter speaks against the cameras at the Village Board, citing "data safety, unauthorized access, privacy violations and abuse, profiling, lack of consent and transparency."

May 24, 2022: the first contract
- The Board approves Flock on the consent agenda, 4 to 0: "12 Automated License Plate reading cameras," at $38,896 the first year and $34,396 a year after.
- The capital request offers "convoy analysis," "associate analysis and identifying vehicles that frequently travel together," and "predictive analytics and historical vehicle location data."
- Funding: "Drug asset forfeiture and DUI forfeiture funds."
- Packet: <https://d3n9y02raazwpg.cloudfront.net/niles/4feca060-14a6-11ec-9f1e-0050569183fa-c24709d9-0e32-4573-adf3-7dc4100ecd8c-1653082004.pdf> (pp. 356 to 358)
- Minutes: <https://niles.granicus.com/services/minutes/reports/a6fb492f-ce1d-4ade-ae28-cd7657d6c4f2/attachment>

May 24, 2022: public comment (Village Board meeting video)
- A commenter tells the Board: "These automatic license plate reader cameras are a violation of our privacy and a threat to people moving about in Niles." He warns the coming overturn of Roe v. Wade "could put women at risk traveling through Illinois." He emailed the Board: "I didn't hear anything back from anybody except the mayor." He says the Board "rammed this through without further input."
- Niles trustees do not usually answer public comment. Trustee Niedermaier broke with that practice. "I've talked with the chief and done my research," he says. "I don't like these cameras because I think we see evidence of abuse everywhere currently." He says the cameras "should have a lot more regulation than they currently have," calls Flock "a passive system currently" that "must be triggered for us to use it," says it is used "largely" for "stolen vehicles and Amber Alerts," and promises "we are going to as a village, as a police force, reevaluate our approach to these cameras every year."
- President Pro Tem Danette O'Donovan Matyas chaired the meeting.
- The commenter asks to respond: "If you're going to grandstand, I would like to be included in this conversation." Trustee Niedermaier shouts him down: "I'm not responding to you. And if you'd like to stick around, we can talk for hours, Chief." and "You had the floor, and now I'm speaking to you." The commenter is told public comment is "not a debate" and "we're asking you if you could just sit down." The next public commenter stepped up. The minutes do not record this exchange.

June and August 2022
- Commenter urge the Board to "mitigate Police surveillance and make Niles an abortion sanctuary" and cite ALPR use against people traveling for abortions.

October 25, 2022
- A public records request seeks Niles Flock records, including emails since March 1, 2022. The Village releases three zip files of emails and withholds "Law Enforcement Sensitive/LEADS data." (<https://www.muckrock.com/foi/multirequest/foia-niles-illinois-pd-flock-safety-documents-oct-2022-114037/>) This request picks up the day after that one was filed.

December 27, 2023
- A police memo reports Flock is raising its price from $2,500 to $3,000 per camera on January 1, 2024, and recommends a new five-year agreement to "lock in our current price."

January 1, 2024
- Illinois' ALPR sharing restrictions take effect (625 ILCS 5/2-130).

January 31, 2024
- Niles' sharing list (Village FOIA 24-75) shows 364 agencies, 43 outside Illinois, including Houston, Texas.
- The same production includes Niles PD Policy 435 (dated January 30, 2024), which allows sharing ALPR data only on a written, approved request kept on file, and requires a signed declaration before any out-of-state sharing.

March 18, 2024
- Asked for every out-of-state declaration since December 1, 2023 (Village FOIA 24-213), the Village answers: "We have no documents related to this request." (<https://www.muckrock.com/foi/niles-8224/alpr-declarations-2024-village-of-niles-illinois-160185/>)

June 2024: the contract is ratified and the network grows
- June 10: the Public Safety Committee recommends 8 more Flock cameras (4 Falcon plate readers, 4 Condor pan/tilt/zoom) paid with a $50,000 state DCEO grant. (<https://www.vniles.com/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Minutes/_06102024-2500>)
- June 25: the Board "ratifies" a revised five-year Flock contract, $177,500 for 2024 to 2029, on the consent agenda, 5 to 0. The order form sets a 30-day retention period, automatic renewal, "Nationwide Network (LP Lookup Only)" and "Community Cameras (Full Access)" to privately owned Flock cameras. (<https://d3n9y02raazwpg.cloudfront.net/niles/ff40e963-90ad-11ee-a93d-0050569183fa-5c0e755c-a6e1-4dab-923d-6341f54990e3-1718996996.pdf>, pp. 534 to 545)

July 2024 to March 2025
- Houston police, one of the 43 out-of-state agencies on Niles' list, run 114 searches of Niles cameras logged "immigration." (Village FOIA 25-313)

January 28, 2025
- A street lighting change order includes "FLOCK POLE ... $8,697.00." (<https://d3n9y02raazwpg.cloudfront.net/niles/2d88d52b-960f-11ef-ab4b-005056a89546-1a926250-3551-4a5b-bb27-9f3f35227c9b-1737755196.pdf>, p. 245)

May 9, 2025: the 2022 warning comes true in Niles
- A Texas sheriff's search logged "had an abortion, search for female" reaches 83,345 cameras, including Niles'. In June 2025 the Illinois Secretary of State announces Illinois cameras were among those reached. (<https://www.axios.com/local/chicago/2025/07/01/illinois-texas-police-data-abortion-law> ; <https://www.404media.co/a-texas-cop-searched-license-plate-cameras-nationwide-for-a-woman-who-got-an-abortion/>)

May 30, 2025: Niles shares with Border Patrol
- Niles' sharing list (Village FOIA 25-313) shows 1,094 agencies, about 630 outside Illinois, plus U.S. Border Patrol and the US Postal Inspection Service.
- June 9, 2025: a "[Federal] US Border Patrol [Inactive]" account runs 24 searches of Niles cameras logged "USBP/HSI."

August 2025
- The Illinois Secretary of State says an audit found U.S. Customs and Border Protection accessed Illinois Flock data, "a clear violation of the state law." Flock pauses its federal pilot programs. (<https://news.wttw.com/node/51786>)

January 27, 2026
- The same commenter from 2022 returns to the Board with "concern about Flock cameras and the sharing of the data with Federal agencies." No response appears in the minutes.

February 11, 2026
- A Niles police commander: "we have a contract with Flock and have some cameras positioned at strategic locations." (<https://www.vniles.com/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Minutes/_02112026-2669>)

April 28, 2026: FY2027 budget
- The Village still budgets $34,396 a year for the program, justified by "access to billions of license plate scans" from "cameras that are deployed in cities throughout the country." (<https://www.vniles.com/DocumentCenter/View/17191>)

October 13, 2026
- The transparency portal lists 21 cameras, 993,334 vehicles in 30 days, and 475 receiving agencies, all in Illinois. (<https://transparency.flocksafety.com/niles-il-pd>)

- IN SUMMARY -

What the public knows about how this system is used comes from activists and independent researchers who have pried audit logs loose one agency at a time, through delays, denials, and logs that arrive with officers' names, plates and filters replaced by asterisks. The searches listed above are only the ones that have become public. They come from sources working as designed: records the state chose to release and press coverage that decided which stories were worth telling. Even so, they show that police are one arm of a larger system of empire, and that ALPR systems are colonizers' weapons on colonized land. That is the part of the story no police department, vendor, newsroom or local government will admit to. Pinning it all on one ALPR vendor gives empire a convenient scapegoat.

Four years in, Niles police still use Flock ALPR cameras, even after opening them to U.S. Border Patrol and hundreds of out-of-state agencies. Nothing in the Village's public record says who approved that, or when and why it stopped. When asked in 2024 for the out-of-state declarations the law requires, the Village said it had none. The public record does not show whether Niles did anything after a Texas abortion search and hundreds of immigration searches swept its cameras, whether anyone reviewed the hundreds of Niles searches logged "zz," whether the "lot more regulation" a trustee called for in 2022 ever arrived, or whether the yearly review he promised ever took place. A community member who asked these questions at the podium was told to sit down, and asked them again four years later to silence.

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Records relating to or mentioning Henry Wadsworth Longfellow Dana (January 26, 1881-April 26, 1950), aka Harry Dana or H. W. L. Dana. Dana was a scholar and educator at Columbia University and the New School for Social Research, among other places. He was a conscientious objector during World War I. He made multiple visits to Soviet Russia during the 1920s and 1930s. He lived most of his life in Cambridge, Massachusetts, and New York, New York.

I believe you have already released documents related to Dana, as some are cited in: Eliza Starr Byard, “Inverts, Perverts, and National Peril: Federal Responses to Homosexuality, 1890–1956 - ProQuest” (Dissertation, Columbia University, 2002).

Please conduct a search of the Central Records System, including but not limited to the ELSUR Records System, the Microphone Surveillance (MISUR) Indices, the Physical Surveillance (FISUR) Indices, and the Technical Surveillance (TESUR) Indices, for both main-file records and cross-reference records for all relevant names, individuals, agencies and companies. If any potentially responsive records have been destroyed and/or transferred to NARA, then I request copies of the destruction or transfer slips as well as any other documentation relating to, mentioning or describing said transfer or destruction, to include but not be limited to confirmation that the Bureau has no other copies of said records (as the Bureau has posted copies of records that it previously said were transferred to NARA such as the Tokyo Rose file).

I am a member of the academic community and request classification as such. I am a PhD Candidate in History at the CUNY Graduate Center, New York, NY. As such, my primary purpose is to use this information to write a dissertation to add to public knowledge and I therefore request that fees be waived. Per DOJ FOIA guidance, "a requester should be granted a fee waiver if the requested information (1) sheds light on the activities and operations of the government; (2) is likely to contribute significantly to public understanding of those operations and activities; and (3) is not primarily in the commercial interest of the requester." As this FOIA meets all of these requirements, a fee waiver is warranted.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Danielle Bennett

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New York Freedom of Information Law, I hereby request the following records:

Records related to the department’s Flock Safety system:

1. Organization Audit in Flock.
For the period January 1, 2024 to the date this request is processed: the Flock Organization Audit report and corresponding retained audit records of searches conducted by users within the Department's organization. Per Flock's documentation, the Organization Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches done within the agency.

2. Network Audit in Flock.
For the period January 1, 2024 to the date this request is processed: the Flock Network Audit report and corresponding retained audit records of searches of the Department's Flock network by any agency in the Flock system. Per Flock's documentation, the Network Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches of the organization’s Flock network by any agency in the Flock System.

For items 1 and 2, please provide all maintained and exportable fields, including, where present, search timestamps, user names and identifiers, organization names and identifiers, search reasons, complaint or case numbers, search types, filters, date ranges searched, and counts of networks or devices searched. The reasons for a search, associated complaint number, and identity of the authorized inquirer are specifically addressed by General Order O-44.13, "Records."

3. Existing electronic records of the Department's inbound and outbound Flock network-sharing configuration as of the date the search for these records is conducted. Include the names and identifiers of organizations sharing their networks with the Department and organizations with which the Department shares its networks, together with the direction and status of each sharing relationship. Please provide existing settings exports or reports, or the underlying electronically retrievable configuration records in an available format.

4. Flock Safety Event Log.
For the period January 1, 2024 to the date this request is processed: the Flock Safety Event Log, including all maintained and exportable fields. Per Flock's documentation, the Event Log is available within the Insights tab. Flock customer support may be able to assist with the mass-downloading of this data if assistance is required.

The Organization Audit, Network Audit, and Event Log are identified by their Flock report names and their availability through the Insights tab. If these reports have been renamed or moved, please provide the equivalent records. Items 1, 2, and 4 seek audit and event records, rather than a bulk export of the underlying vehicle-sighting database or camera images.

Records relating to the Department's ALPR policy:

5.  All versions of written policies governing the deployment of automated license plate recognition cameras/readers/systems and the use, storage, retention, and sharing of data obtained through those systems that were created, revised, or in effect at any time from January 1, 2024 to the date this request is processed. Include General Order O-44.13, applicable predecessor policies, amendments, and existing records showing each version's effective date and review date. Include policies adopted before January 1, 2024 if they remained in effect during any part of the requested period.

6. For the period January 1, 2024 to the date this request is processed: all records of completed audits of ALPR system usage including any audit reports, findings, worksheets, spreadsheets, checklists, reviewer notes, sampling methodology, and corrective-action recommendations. This includes records of the regular audits required by General Order O-44.13, "Records," and corresponding audits conducted under predecessor ALPR policies. This item seeks records of completed compliance audits and reviews, distinct from the underlying automated logs requested in items 1, 2, and 4.

7. For the period January 1, 2024 to the date this request is processed: all existing records concerning initial and refresher ALPR training provided to Department personnel, including Department-conducted and vendor-provided workshops, meetings, demonstrations, webinars, and other training sessions. This includes meeting notices and invitations, schedules, agendas, session dates and locations, instructor and training-provider information, registration records, attendance rosters, sign-in sheets, completion records and certificates, lesson plans, curricula, presentations, handouts, training bulletins, and any retained recordings. The request includes training on operation and configuration of the ALPR system, access to and use of ALPR data, Department policy and procedures, applicable laws, and privacy protections, as addressed by General Order O-44.13, "Training," and corresponding training under predecessor ALPR policies. Include existing records of Department approval of those training programs and refresher training addressing system updates, changes in law, or policy revisions.

8. For the period January 1, 2020 to the date this request is processed: all emails received from or sent to email addresses ending in @flocksafety.com", and any PDF materials, presentation slides, or other electronic or written materials regarding Flock Safety products received by mail or email by the Police Department.

This request seeks existing retained records, including responsive records maintained in Flock or another service on the Department's behalf. It does not ask the Department to create new policies, agreements, audit findings, training records, or narrative summaries. Where no pre-compiled report exists, please retrieve or extract existing electronic records or data that can be retrieved with reasonable effort, as provided by Public Officers Law Section 89(3)(a).

Please provide records electronically in their native or existing machine-readable export format where available. For tabular audit, event, and configuration records, CSV or spreadsheet files are preferred to PDF printouts or screenshots. Please retain column headings and timestamps as maintained. For other records, please provide the existing electronic files, including responsive email attachments.

If any record or portion is withheld, please identify the specific statutory exemption relied upon, explain its application, and disclose all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions. If particular entries or fields in an audit or event log are properly exempt, please redact those portions rather than withhold the entire report.

Please address each numbered item separately. For records the Department does not possess or cannot locate after a diligent search, please provide the certification contemplated by Public Officers Law Section 89(3)(a), identifying the relevant request item.

Please provide responsive records on a rolling basis as they become available and advise me in advance of any proposed charges.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Scott Conway

title: Records concerning the proposed rescission of the 2001 Roadless Area Conservation Rule

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Records concerning the proposed rescission of the 2001 Roadless Area Conservation Rule
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All records from the U.S. Forest Service concerning the proposal to rescind or revise the 2001 Roadless Area Conservation Rule, including the June 23, 2025 notice of intent and the August 20, 2026 proposed rulemaking and draft environmental impact statement. For all items below, "communications" and "correspondence" include emails, text messages, instant messages, and chat messages (such as Microsoft Teams or Slack), whether sent or received on government-issued or personal devices and accounts used for official business:

1. All communications, memoranda, briefing papers, and decision documents, dated June 1, 2025 to the present, (a) within the Forest Service, (b) between the Forest Service and the USDA Office of the Secretary, and (c) between Forest Service officials and White House or Executive Office of the President officials, concerning the proposed rescission. Please include records from the Office of the Chief, the National Forest System deputy area, and Ecosystem Management Coordination staff involved in the rulemaking. Suggested search terms: "Roadless Rule," "Roadless Area Conservation Rule," "rescission," "inventoried roadless areas," "DEIS."

2. All records reflecting the Forest Service's tabulation, analysis, or summary of public comments received in response to (a) the June 2025 notice of intent and (b) the August 2026 proposed rulemaking, including methodology documents, contractor reports or deliverables related to comment processing, and internal presentations summarizing comment results.

3. All briefing materials, talking points, and decision memoranda prepared for Forest Service or USDA leadership recommending a preferred alternative (including full rescission) in the draft EIS or proposed rule, dated January 1, 2026 to the present.

4. All correspondence (letters, emails, text and instant messages, chat messages, meeting notes or summaries) between Forest Service officials and non-governmental outside parties, including timber industry associations, trade groups, and state government officials, concerning the proposed rescission, dated June 1, 2025 to the present.

Please provide responsive records electronically (searchable PDF or native files). If any records are withheld in whole or in part, please identify each one, state the specific FOIA exemption claimed, and release all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions. I am willing to pay up to $50 in fees; please notify me in advance with an itemized estimate if charges will exceed that amount.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Jeff

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Hiring Board Records & Selection Metrics: Announcement ES_1786461208616 (AFLCMC/ESGH)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

ATTN: Hill AFB FOIA Requester Service Center (66 ABG/CEOE) & Hanscom AFB FOIA Requester Service Center

ACTION REQUIRED: This request concerns a Geographically Separated Unit (AFLCMC/ESGH) located at Hill AFB, UT, reporting to a parent command (AFLCMC/ESG) at Hanscom AFB. Please route to both installations to prevent processing delays.

This is a request under the Freedom of Information Act. I am requesting records regarding the hiring action, evaluation process, and selection board metrics for position announcement tracking number ES_1786461208616, for the NH-04 Deputy Branch Chief / Chief of Logistics position within the AFLCMC/ESGH Branch. AFLCMC/ESGH operates as a Geographically Separated Unit (GSU) located at Hill Air Force Base, UT, under the organizational structure of AFLCMC/ESG based at Hanscom Air Force Base.
The hiring board for this action was comprised of Patrik Caron, Brendan Shaw, and Joey Wilkinson.
To narrow the scope and ensure a prompt response, I am requesting the following specific agency records associated with this announcement:
1. Position Requirements & Minimum Certifications:
	• The formal core personnel document (CPD), position description (PD), and specific evaluation criteria used by the board to determine minimum eligibility.
	• Please explicitly include the mandated thresholds for:
		• Minimum formal educational degrees or equivalent.
		• Time-in-Grade (TIG) restrictions or equivalent corporate experience required for an NH-04 appointment.
		• Required Professional Military Education (PME) levels.
		• Defense Acquisition University (DAU) / Defense Acquisition Workforce Improvement Act (DAWIA) Lifecycle Logistics certification levels (e.g., Back-to-Basics foundational or advanced tiers).
2. Anonymized Selection & Interview Statistics:
	• The total number of applicants who submitted packages for listing ES_1786461208616.
	• The total number of applicants determined by Human Resources to meet the basic qualifications.
	• The total number of applicants who were referred to the hiring board and subsequently selected for an interview.
3. Board Evaluation, Grading Matrices, and Scoreheets:
	• All blank templates, scorecards, evaluation rubrics, and grading sheets utilized by panel members Patrik Caron, Brendan Shaw, and Joey Wilkinson to rate candidates during the interview and portfolio review phases.
	• All anonymized, completed grading sheets, master tally sheets, ranking rosters, or merit promotion certificates generated by the board. (Note: To protect personal privacy under Exemption 6, applicant names may be redacted and replaced with anonymous identifiers, e.g., "Candidate A," "Candidate B").
4. Selection Justification & Discrepancy Records:
	• The final selection justification memo or formal recommendation signed by the board members detailing the rationale for the final selection.
	• Any memoranda, emails, or internal board correspondence discussing adjustments to scores, exceptions made for certification shortfalls, or tie-breaking justifications where a candidate with less seniority, lower DAU certification levels, or fewer baseline qualifications was selected over higher-scoring or more experienced applicants on the referral list.

Fee Waiver & Processing:
I request that all processing fees be waived as this matter directly concerns the transparency, fairness, and administrative integrity of civil service hiring practices within Air Force Materiel Command. If fees cannot be waived, please notify me if costs are projected to exceed $25.00.
If any portion of this request is withheld under a dynamic interpretation of FOIA exemptions, please release all reasonably segregable, non-exempt portions.
Thank you for your time and assistance. I look forward to your prompt response within the statutory 20-business-day window.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FEDERAL ACQUISITION & LOGISTICS WATCH

communications.communication:
"Dear A. Gray:

Thank you for your interest in public records of Jackson County. Your request has been received and is being processed in accordance with the Missouri Sunshine Law. Your request was received in this office on 10/11/2026 and given the reference number R009800-101126 for tracking purposes.

Records Requested: To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the The Missouri Sunshine Law, I hereby request the following records:

All reports generated by the Jackson County Sheriff's Office concerning conduct or incidents on the premises of the establishment located at 2111 Television Pl, Kansas City, MO, 64126, from the year 2000 until the present.

The Jackson County Sheriff's Office was called to the premises of 2111 Television Pl 100 times between 2016 and 2022 for events including, but not limited to, noise complaints, shootings, health code violations, theft and rape.

I understand that many of the responsive records may contain sensitive, confidential information. I request that any personal information be redacted from records which contain personal or otherwise un-releasable information. Alleged conduct at this address, and the response from the Jackson County Sheriff's Office and other law enforcement agencies, have both been the subject of extensive public reporting and inquiry. A Kansas City Star article from March 27, 2023 has been added for context.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 3 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

A. Gray

https://cdn.muckrock.com/outbound_composer_attachments/dagrandegringo/187887/article_concering_2111_Television_Pl_Kansas_City_MO_64126.pdf
Upload documents directly: https://www.muckrock.com/respond/2425109/

Your request will be forwarded to the relevant department(s) to locate the information you seek and to determine the volume and any costs associated with satisfying your request. You will be contacted about the availability and/or provided with copies of the records in question. PLEASE NOTE: Missouri Sunshine Law does not require a governmental body to create new information, to do legal research, or to answer questions.

You can monitor the progress of your request at the link below and you'll receive an email when your request has been completed. Again, thank you for using the Public Records Center.

Jackson County"

The complete current contract, all purchase orders, and any amendments or renewals with Flock
Safety Inc. or any ALPR vendor — including the total cost, contract term, payment schedule, and any
automatic renewal provisions.

The complete written policy governing how long license plate images, timestamps, location data, and
associated metadata are retained before deletion.

Any written policy, general order, directive, or memorandum of understanding governing who may
conduct searches of ALPR data and what justification is required before a search may be run.

A complete list of every agency outside Safford, AZ — including local, county, state, federal, or out-of-
state agencies — that has been granted access to or has queried Safford, AZ ALPR data, along with
copies of any data-sharing agreements, memoranda of understanding, or written authorizations.
6. AUDITS AND REVIEWS
Any internal review, third-party audit, inspector general report, or other formal assessment of ALPR
system use, access patterns, data security, or potential misuse.
7. COMMUNICATIONS WITH FLOCK SAFETY
All written communications between Safford, AZ, officials and Flock Safety Inc. representatives
concerning: data sharing, the Flock national network, system audits, access by outside agencies,
immigration enforcement, civil liberties, or public records requests — for the period
1/1/2024-10/1/2026.
